title: Security review - data residency & region pinning
summary: Customer high-level requirement: EU-only processing for PHI-adjacent metadata, strict no-cross-border for inference, prefer region pinning to eu-west-1, request for SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 artifacts and BYOK/KMS options. Redwood to provide SOC2 report, sub-processor list, data flow diagram, and draft DPA; schedule POC to validate region pinning and latency. Legal to confirm wording on subprocessors and breach notification SLA.
topics: Region pinning / dedicated routing to eu-west-1
Audit logs, retention, and access controls (RBAC, SSO)
SOC2/ISO artifacts and pen test summary
action_items: Maya: send SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 cert copy by 2025-10-24
Liam: prepare technical note on region pinning implementation and expected latency delta by 2025-10-27
Maya: share sub-processor spreadsheet and third-party locations (AWS GCP) by 2025-10-24
Redwood infra (Liam): provide data flow diagram showing EU-only flow and where cache/kv may live by 2025-10-28
Sara (Novus): draft list of legal questions on DPA and subprocessors due 2025-10-29
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and sub-processor list (Maya)
Schedule 1-week POC to test region pinning in eu-west-1 and measure latency (Liam/Maya to coordinate)
Customer legal to review DPA with subprocessors clause and provide questions
Follow-up call to review POC results and finalize contract terms (tentative 2025-11-05)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha Khan (Novus): Aisha here, Head of Security.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: Marco - platform. Tom joining from DevOps. Sara from legal is on.
[00:18] Maya: Great. Liam from Redwood is here for the technical bits. we'll mostly focus on data residency, region pinning, and subprocessors.
[00:28] Liam Patel (Redwood SE): Hi all. quick warning, my audio might pop if I switch networks.
[00:32] Aisha: no worries. to set expectations, Novus needs EU-only processing for any metadata or outputs that are PHI-adjacent. We have strict cross-border rules.
[00:42] Maya: Understood. can you clarify whether you need both storage and inference to stay in EU, or just storage?
[00:49] Aisha: Both. inference and any transient tokens — we cannot allow routing to US for processing.
[00:54] Marco: we also want region pinning so requests from EU always hit eu-west-1 endpoints.
[01:02] Liam: ok. we support region pinning in our platform — we can route by policy to a regional cluster. there is an implementation caveat: some managed services (monitoring/logging third-party) may be in partner regions unless we use dedicated stacks.
[01:18] Sara (Legal): can you confirm subprocessors and where they store logs?
[01:23] Maya: yes — we'll share a sub-processor list. quick note: our usual sub-processors include AWS (eu-west-1 primary for EU), GCP in europe-west1 for some components, and Datadog for telemetry. some backups and analytics may by default land in us-east-1 unless we opt into EU-only plan.
[01:40] Aisha: that's a red flag for us. we need strict assurances and preferably BYOK so we control keys.
[01:47] Liam: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations and we can configure to use an EU KMS region. note: BYOK covers data at rest but transit and processing still occur in the compute region — which we can pin.
[02:02] Tom: are audit logs retained in the EU as well?
[02:06] Maya: default retention is in the same region as the control plane for private deployments; for hosted customers we can route logs to region-locked S3 buckets as part of an enterprise package.
[02:18] Marco: what's the difference between a hosted EU-only plan and Redwood Dedicated on this front?
[02:24] Liam: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and control — you can provision a dedicated pool strictly in eu-west-1 with network controls. hosted EU-only is possible but sometimes involves our multi-tenant control plane in US - though we can provide a private control plane option for enterprise. in practice, for strict regulators we recommend either Dedicated or Private deployments.
[02:44] Aisha: we prefer not to have a control plane in US; can you do a private control plane in EU?
[02:48] Maya: yes, we offer a private control plane and on-prem options where required — that'll be part of the enterprise package.
[02:55] Sara: about breach notification timelines, what SLAs do you have?
[02:59] Maya: we have contractual breach notification windows in our standard DPA; typically 72 hours for confirmed incidents. we can escalate for PHI-adjacent incidents per contract.
[03:12] Sara: ok we'll want that in the DPA.
[03:16] Liam: a few technical points: region pinning uses smart routing and can be configured per-customer or per-route. we can also do per-model routing — e.g., use a quantized smaller model in EU if needed. caching — our prefix/KV cache can be configured to persist in-region. but a gotcha: if you enable cross-region failover for resilience, you must accept potential cross-border processing in those failover scenarios.
[03:44] Marco: so no cross-region failover then. we will prioritize strict locality over cross-region HA in initial scope.
[03:51] Liam: understood. that reduces complexity. for monitoring and tracing, we can offer an EU-only telemetry pipeline, but that requires opting into our enterprise telemetry plan and possibly replacing Datadog with a EU-located tenant.
[04:06] Aisha: are pen test reports and SOC2 Type II available?
[04:10] Maya: yes — SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts exist; I'll share copy of the latest report and summary of penetration test coverage.
[04:18] Sara: also need third-party attestation around subprocessors — where are your backups and metrics streamed?
[04:24] Maya: backups for EU customers can be restricted to EU S3 buckets; metrics may go to third-party telemetry — we can configure ingestion to EU telemetry providers. we'll put this in the sub-processor spreadsheet.
[04:36] Marco: curious about BYOK - if we bring our own key in EU, can you guarantee keys never leave region?
[04:42] Liam: yes, if you use a regional KMS we can configure the key material to reside in eu-west-1. note though that some orchestration metadata may be in the control plane; with private control plane that can be in EU as well.
[04:57] Aisha: what's the expected latency overhead to run in eu-west-1 vs default multi-region?
[05:01] Liam: negligible in-region; default multi-region sometimes uses US GPUs for scaling which adds 80-200ms depending on workload. we'll include a short benchmark with numbers for your typical seq lengths.
[05:13] Maya: we should schedule a short POC to validate pinning and also measure tokenizer coverage and latency on your prompts.
[05:20] Marco: yes we'd like that.
[05:23] Liam: technical caveat — certain open-source model variants we optimize for may depend on kernel availability; we can provide EU GPU images but quantization profiles might change. we'll document that.
[05:40] Tom: any subcontractors outside of EU that could process data transiently (e.g., model fine-tuning or bench jobs)?
[05:48] Maya: no fine-tuning by default for Hosted; we don't send customer data for training. for analytics and some ops, yes — but for your EU-only request we'll opt out of analytics exports and ensure no training loop.
[06:00] Aisha: good. please put that in writing.
[06:03] Maya: will do.
[06:05] Sara: also want RBAC and SSO details — we use SAML 2.0 and expect SCIM provisioning.
[06:12] Liam: we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning users; RBAC roles can be scoped to teams and you can set token-level role restrictions. audit logs show API key usage and user actions; retention configurable for enterprise.
[06:26] Marco: is there an immutable audit trail for admin actions?
[06:29] Liam: yes we have append-only logs with retention policies; for customers with strict eDiscovery we can provide log exports to your SIEM in EU.
[06:39] Aisha: what about subpoena / law enforcement requests? if control plane is US, could data be subject to US legal process?
[06:46] Maya: yes that's why many customers choose private control plane or Dedicated EU stacks to avoid US jurisdiction. we'll outline options and legal mitigations in the DPA and data flow diagrams.
[06:58] Sara: please include model variants and whether any inference paths use hosted third-party models (eg a proprietary model hosted in US).
[07:05] Liam: we can guarantee that any inference you route to the EU pinned cluster will use EU-hosted model assets. we'll document model storage locations.
[07:14] Maya: i realize we're covering a lot — for the next steps: i'll send SOC2, sub-processor list, and a proposed POC scope. Liam will draft the technical note. legal to send the DPA questions.
[07:26] Aisha: timeline: we aim to onboard pilot within November if everything aligns.
[07:30] Maya: sounds good.
[07:33] [10:12] — mid-call deep dive on technical network flows (notes omitted for brevity) — timestamps continue
[10:12] Liam: digging into routing: request comes in to our edge which does geo-check and then routes to the regional load balancer pinned to eu-west-1. we use continuous batching and a kv cache which we can localize. occasional ops jobs may need ephemeral access to S3 for snapshots; those will be EU buckets for your account.
[11:02] Marco: can you lock down egress so there's no outbound to US?
[11:06] Liam: yes, with Dedicated or Private we can restrict egress CIDR and firewall all outbound endpoints.
[12:00] Aisha: how often do subprocessors change? we need notification.
[12:04] Maya: we update sub-processor list quarterly and will notify changes; we can add contract clause for notice period.
[12:16] Sara: for the DPA we need breach notification, subprocessors list, data flow, and choice of law.
[12:22] Maya: noted. we'll work with legal.
[12:26] [20:00] — discussion on KMS and BYOK steps —
[20:05] Liam: BYOK handshake is simple: you create a key in your EU KMS, give us key ARN and we integrate via cross-account grant; we never export key material. rotation and revocation policies remain with you.
[20:26] Tom: any ops book for revoking keys and emergency access?
[20:30] Liam: yes we have runbooks; we'll include a condensed version in the POC package.
[30:00] — questions about audit log retention and SIEM integration —
[30:10] Maya: export to your SIEM can be via secure, signed transfer into your EU tenant; retention TTLs are configurable.
[30:36] Aisha: what's the standard log retention?
[30:40] Liam: default 90 days for hosted, enterprise can go to 7 years with archival in encrypted EU storage.
[40:00] — legal redlines and DPA conversation —
[40:12] Sara: we'll need vendor answers inline in the DPA plus subprocessors attachment.
[40:18] Maya: we'll provide that and a draft DPA clause samples.
[45:00] — wrap up and recapping next steps —
[45:10] Maya: to recap: i will send SOC2/ISO artifacts and sub-processor list; liam will produce region pinning technical note and KV/cache locality doc; we'll propose a POC in eu-west-1; legal will send DPA questions.
[45:30] Aisha: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[45:33] Marco: looking forward to the POC.
[45:36] Sara: expecting SOC2 and sub-processor list this week.
[45:40] Maya: yes aim for EOD Friday (2025-10-24).
[51:50] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and book the POC slot once we have a go from legal. bye.
[51:57] Meeting ended.
